To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mobility of the T cell receptor (a key molecule involved in T cell recognition of antigens) is decreased when intracellular calcium levels are raised, and this is dependent on a functional cytoskeleton.
the lateral diffusion of TCR on T lymphocytes can be reduced by pharmacological treatments that cause an increase of intracellular calcium and actin polymerization.
an increase in intrcellular calcium levels causes a decrease in T cell receptor lateral mobility, and that this effect is dependent on a functional cytoskeleton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the TCR during the formation of the immunological synapses.
the effects of intracellular calcium on the mobility of surface molecules, and in particular, the T cell receptor.
the dynamics of the TCR and the cytoskeleton during T cell activation, and provides new insight into the mechanisms of T cell activation
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCR mobility decreases in the presence of calcium, and that the actin cyoskeleton plays a key role in this effect.
the TCR/cytokkeleton binding is increased by the calcium induced polymerization of the cytoskeleton and this binding reduces the TCR mobility.
TCRs move more slowly when they interact with the actin cyteskeleton and this interaction is increased by calcium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the actin cyoskeleton can be regulated by intracellular calcium and that it has an effect on the TCR mobility.
TCR mobility is reduced by an increase in intracytoplasmic calcium, which is dependent on the actin cyto-skeleton.
TCR motion in the plane of the membrane is affected by the intracellular calcium concentration and by the polymerization state of the actin network.

TCR mobility can be reduced by an increase in intracytosolic calcium levels.
the mobility of TCRs is regulated by the intracellular calcium levels and the actin filament network.
the mobility of TCRs is regulated by intracellular calcium and the actin-cytoskeleton.
